newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Sellers ride on U.S. strength.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Sellers ride on U.S. strength.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices were flat but sellers have edged up their offers on the back of firmer U.S. prices, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"It's been pretty uninspiring," one producer said.
"Prices are flat...there has been no change in the past two weeks," he added.
Sources said buyers indicated around $250 per tonne for free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting in June lifting, around last week's levels of $245 and $255.
But producers were only offering at $260.
"Sellers are riding on the strength of the U.S.," a trader said.
Traders said with the arbitrage window to the U.S. West Coast at around $255 to $257 fob Singapore, at least one trader is seeking to buy cargoes.
"But the producers won't entertain the buyer... they would rather move the cargoes themselves," a trader said.
Sources said demand has been lacklustre and they were looking towards Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) July tender results, due late Wednesday, to provide firmer direction.
CPC's regular monthly tender to buy 3,500 to 7,000-tonnes for delivery July 6-20 to Kaohsiung or Keelung, closes May 27.
Some traders expected the award to be higher than CPC's last award for June 10-24 delivery, to Italian producer Ecofuel at $267 per tonne, c-and-f Taiwan.
"Most producers will only go higher because of the U.S.," a trader said.

But other traders said with very thin demand from gasoline blenders and from Indonesia ahead of tomorrow's elections, they expected producers to offer very aggressively into Taiwan at around $263-$264.
Traders largely discounted news that the 700,000 tonne-per-year Sadaf plant, originally scheduled for start-up last August, is now scheduled to start up in early June.
The facility is a joint venture between Royal/Dutch Shell and Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
